The filter is an exact replacement for the factory unit and is working as advertised. So easy to install. Remove the old one with a counter clockwise turn to the stop and pull out. I had only a few drops of waters escape. Insert the new one and turn clockwise to the stop, about 1/2 turn, you may hear the water surge into the filter.

The filtering agent is charcoal so run several tea glasses of water through before you drink. You will see a slight grey tint to the water at first. That is any charcoal dust that was present. By the third glass I was getting perfectly clear and completely tasteless drinking water. I am buying several more backups.

No matter how much water I flush thru the filter it still looks like a glass of salt water...cloudy and grey. Even after letting it settle for a bit there's a film of something floating at the top of the glass. I let the filter sit overnight and tried flushing it again. No luck. Returning it and buying one that I know works. What a hassle!

After purchasing our new home, we realized the previous owner had seemingly never changed the water filter in the refrigerator. Living in an unincorporated area, we have well water, so any extra treatment the water can have is well worth it. After doing some research and discovering how much the OEM filters cost, I was disappointed. It's a water filter, for goodness sake. It shouldn't cost as much as a decent night out with my wife.

After reading lots of reviews on Amazon, I was again disappointed. Some were seemed decent, but then had loads of terrible reviews. Then I finally happened upon this brand. After combing through the reviews, I felt confident in giving it a shot. So I placed my order and, to my surprise, the filter was at my door the very next day. Not even 24 hours later.

Installation was simple (honestly, it's almost impossible to mess up this step...) and after running a few gallons of water through the filter, I could immediately tell a difference with the quality of water, as compared to it being run through the old filter. I will definitely be purchasing my future water filters through Waterfall.

I have bought 2 of these and am going to order a third one now, if that tells you anything.  I give it 5 stars for being as good as the one that came in my Kitchenaid dishwasher if not better, but 3 for still not being good enough that it can handle the heat  and not have the bottom break out.  I've had one last for over a year and the one I bought for my mom only lasted 6 months.  I think her DW is a Kenmore.  I do like that it is half the price of replacing it with the Kitchenaid one.  One trick I have found to make it last a bit longer is to take the top cover off and place it underneath the basket in your dishwasher.  That gives it a little bit more distance between it and the elements and it also helps for when you do get holes in the bottom to keep things inside.
